| text |  Four changes: `signup.html` (widget), `app.py` (server-side verify), `.env.example` (new keys), `requirements.txt` (requests library). Let's do them all.<br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br>Now add the captcha margin CSS — just a small spacing fix so the widget doesn't sit flush against the confirm field:<br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br>Now update `app.py` — the signup route needs to verify the hCaptcha token with hCaptcha's API before creating the account:<br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br><br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br>Now add the hCaptcha verify helper right after `load_dotenv()`:<br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br><br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br>Now update the signup route to verify the token and pass the site key to the template:<br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br><br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br><br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br>Now update `.env.example` and `requirements.txt`:<br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br><br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br><br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br>Here's a summary of every change and the reasoning behind each decision.<br><br>---<br><br>**`signup.html`** — two additions. The `<div class="h-captcha">` is where hCaptcha renders its widget. The `data-sitekey` attribute is filled from `{{ hcaptcha_site_key }}` which the route passes in — this key is public and safe to appear in HTML. The hCaptcha JS (`api.js`) is loaded in the scripts block with `async defer` so it doesn't block page rendering. When the user completes the challenge, hCaptcha injects a hidden input named `h-captcha-response` into the form automatically — your backend reads that field.<br><br>**`app.py`** — three additions. `requests` is imported as `http_requests` (avoids any name collision with Flask's `request`). The `verify_hcaptcha()` helper POSTs the token to `https://api.hcaptcha.com/siteverify` with your secret key and checks the `success` field in the JSON response. It returns `False` on any network error — this is "fail closed", meaning if hCaptcha's API is unreachable, signups are blocked rather than waved through. In the signup route, the token is read from `request.form.get("h-captcha-response")` and verified independently of the other field checks — this is intentional so all errors show at once rather than making the user fix username/password and then hit the captcha error separately.<br><br>**`.env.example`** — two new keys. `HCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` goes in the HTML (public). `HCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` never leaves the server. Both come from your hCaptcha dashboard.<br><br>**`requirements.txt`** — `requests` added for the server-side API call.<br><br>---<br><br>**Getting your keys (two minutes):**<br><br>1. Go to [dashboard.hcaptcha.com](https://dashboard.hcaptcha.com) and create a free account<br>2. Add a new site — enter `nbookshelf.ddns.net` as the hostname<br>3. Copy the **Site Key** and **Secret Key**<br>4. On your VM: `sudo nano /srv/bookshelf/.env` and fill in both values<br>5. Deploy: `git push && ./deploy/deploy.sh` |

| 31 |  |  |  | [] |  |  |  | null |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 2026-06-26T13:23:37.221925Z | 2026-06-26T13:23:49.280730Z |  | Here's a summary of every change and the reasoning behind each decision.<br><br>---<br><br>**`signup.html`** — two additions. The `<div class="h-captcha">` is where hCaptcha renders its widget. The `data-sitekey` attribute is filled from `{{ hcaptcha_site_key }}` which the route passes in — this key is public and safe to appear in HTML. The hCaptcha JS (`api.js`) is loaded in the scripts block with `async defer` so it doesn't block page rendering. When the user completes the challenge, hCaptcha injects a hidden input named `h-captcha-response` into the form automatically — your backend reads that field.<br><br>**`app.py`** — three additions. `requests` is imported as `http_requests` (avoids any name collision with Flask's `request`). The `verify_hcaptcha()` helper POSTs the token to `https://api.hcaptcha.com/siteverify` with your secret key and checks the `success` field in the JSON response. It returns `False` on any network error — this is "fail closed", meaning if hCaptcha's API is unreachable, signups are blocked rather than waved through. In the signup route, the token is read from `request.form.get("h-captcha-response")` and verified independently of the other field checks — this is intentional so all errors show at once rather than making the user fix username/password and then hit the captcha error separately.<br><br>**`.env.example`** — two new keys. `HCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` goes in the HTML (public). `HCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` never leaves the server. Both come from your hCaptcha dashboard.<br><br>**`requirements.txt`** — `requests` added for the server-side API call.<br><br>---<br><br>**Getting your keys (two minutes):**<br><br>1. Go to [dashboard.hcaptcha.com](https://dashboard.hcaptcha.com) and create a free account<br>2. Add a new site — enter `nbookshelf.ddns.net` as the hostname<br>3. Copy the **Site Key** and **Secret Key**<br>4. On your VM: `sudo nano /srv/bookshelf/.env` and fill in both values<br>5. Deploy: `git push && ./deploy/deploy.sh` |  | text |

| json_block | {"language": "python", "code": "\nload_dotenv()\n\napp = Flask(__name__)\napp.secret_key = os.environ[\"SECRET_KEY\"]\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Session cookie security \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n# Once HTTPS is confirmed working, set FORCE_HTTPS=true in .env.\n# This makes the session cookie HTTPS-only \u2014 it will never be sent over\n# plain HTTP, which protects login sessions from being intercepted.\napp.config.update(\n    SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True,                              # JS can never read the cookie\n    SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=\"Lax\",                              # basic CSRF protection\n    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=os.environ.get(\"FORCE_HTTPS\", \"false\").lower() == \"true\",\n)\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 DB helpers \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\ndef get_db():\n    if \"db\" not in g:\n        g.db = psycopg2.connect(\n            host=os.environ[\"DB_HOST\"],\n            port=os.environ[\"DB_PORT\"],\n            dbname=os.environ[\"DB_NAME\"],\n", "filename": "/mnt/user-data/outputs/app.py"} |

| text |  <br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br><br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br>Also add `ADMIN_EMAIL` to `.env.example` so it's documented but not filled in:<br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br><br>```<br>This block is not supported on your current device yet.<br>```<br><br>Two changes, and what each does:<br><br>**`curl -4`** — forces curl to resolve `ifconfig.me` over IPv4 and get back an IPv4 address. Without it, on a dual-stack VM curl can return an IPv6 address while `dig` returns an IPv4 one, causing a false mismatch warning even when DNS is correct.<br><br>**`ADMIN_EMAIL` from `.env`** — the script now reads the email at the top before doing anything else, using `grep` + `sed` to extract just the value and strip any surrounding quotes or spaces. If the file doesn't exist or the key is missing, the script exits immediately with a clear error message telling you exactly what to add. The `.env` on your VM is never committed to git, so the email stays private. The `.env.example` in the repo shows the key name with a placeholder value — enough for anyone reading the repo to know it's needed, without exposing a real address.<br><br>**What to do on the VM before re-running the script:**<br><br>```bash<br>sudo nano /srv/bookshelf/.env<br># Add this line with your real email:<br># ADMIN_EMAIL=you@example.com<br>```<br><br>Then run as before:<br>```bash<br>sudo bash setup_https.sh<br>``` |

| json_block | {"language": "bash", "code": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# deploy/setup_https.sh\n#\n# ONE-TIME script to enable HTTPS for nbookshelf.ddns.net using\n# Let's Encrypt (via Certbot) and your existing Nginx config.\n#\n# Run this ON THE VM, after Nginx is already serving the site over plain HTTP:\n#   scp deploy/setup_https.sh ubuntu@YOUR_VM_IP:~\n#   ssh ubuntu@YOUR_VM_IP\n#   chmod +x setup_https.sh\n#   sudo bash setup_https.sh\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nDOMAIN=\"nbookshelf.ddns.net\"\n\necho \"==> [1/4] Confirming DNS resolves correctly\"\nRESOLVED_IP=$(dig +short \"$DOMAIN\" \| tail -n1)\nMY_IP=$(curl -s ifconfig.me)\necho \"    $DOMAIN resolves to: $RESOLVED_IP\"\necho \"    This VM's public IP: $MY_IP\"\nif [ \"$RESOLVED_IP\" != \"$MY_IP\" ]; then\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"    WARNING: DNS does not point to this VM yet.\"\n    echo \"    Let's Encrypt verification will fail until this matches.\"\n    echo \"    Check your DuckDNS/No-IP dashboard and try again.\"\n    read -p \"    Continue anyway? (y/N) \" confirm\n    [ \"$confirm\" = \"y\" ] \|\| exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"==> [2/4] Installing Certbot\"\napt-get update -qq\napt-get install -y -qq certbot python3-certbot-nginx\n\necho \"==> [3/4] Requesting certificate and configuring Nginx\"\n# --nginx plugin edits your existing config automatically:\n#   - adds a 443 server block with the cert paths filled in\n#   - adds an HTTP -> HTTPS redirect on port 80\n#   - reloads nginx for you\ncertbot --nginx \\\n    -d \"$DOMAIN\" \\\n    --non-interactive \\\n    --agree-tos \\\n    --redirect \\\n    -m \"your-email@example.com\"   # <-- replace with a real email for renewal alerts\n\necho \"==> [4/4] Verifying auto-renewal is scheduled\"\nsystemctl list-timers \| grep certbot \|\| echo \"    (certbot.timer should appear above; if not, check: systemctl status certbot.timer)\"\n\necho \"\"\necho \"\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\"\necho \"  HTTPS is live: https://$DOMAIN\"\necho \"\"\necho \"  Certificates auto-renew via systemd timer \u2014 nothing\"\necho \"  further to do. Test renewal with:\"\necho \"     sudo certbot renew --dry-run\"\necho \"\"\necho \"  Next: set FORCE_HTTPS=true in /srv/bookshelf/.env\"\necho \"  then: sudo systemctl restart bookshelf\"\necho \"\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\u2550\"\n", "filename": "/mnt/user-data/outputs/deploy/setup_https.sh"} |

Enable the People API**<br>Sidebar → **APIs & Services → Library** → search `Google People API` → Enable. (Needed for the userinfo endpoint.)<br><br>**3. Configure the OAuth consent screen**<br>Sidebar → **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen**<br>- User type: **External**<br>- App name: `Bookshelf`<br>- User support email: your email<br>- Authorised domain: `ddns.net` (the root domain of your DDNS hostname)<br>- Developer contact: your email<br>- Scopes → **Add or remove scopes** → add `email` and `profile`<br>- Save. Leave it in **Testing** mode — you can add yourself as a test user and it works immediately without Google review.<br><br>**4. Create OAuth credentials**<br>Sidebar → **APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID**<br>- Application type: **Web application**<br>- Name: `Bookshelf VM`<br>- Authorised redirect URIs — add exactly:<br>  ```<br>  https://nbookshelf.ddns.net/auth/google/callback<br>  ```<br>- Click Create → copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**<br><br>**5. Add to your VM's `.env`**<br>```bash<br>ssh ubuntu@YOUR_VM_IP<br>sudo nano /srv/bookshelf/.env<br># Add:<br># GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com<br># GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret<br>```<br><br>---<br><br>## Deploy steps<br><br>```bash<br># Run the DB migration (adds email + google_id columns)<br>ssh ubuntu@YOUR_VM_IP<br>psql -U bookshelf_user -d bookshelf_db -h localhost \<br>     -f /srv/bookshelf/deploy/migrate_google_oauth.sql<br><br># Push code and deploy<br>git add .<br>git commit -m "Add Google OAuth"<br>git push origin main<br>./deploy/deploy.sh<br>```<br><br>---<br><br>## What changed and why<br><br>**`schema.sql` + `migrate_google_oauth.sql`** — `users` gains two new nullable columns. `google_id` is Google's stable `sub` identifier — it never changes even if the user changes their email or name. `email` is used for account linking. Both are `UNIQUE` with indexes. `password_hash` is now nullable to support Google-only users who never set a password.<br><br>**`app.py`** — two new routes. `/auth/google` builds the redirect URL to Google's consent screen and stores a random `state` token in the session to prevent CSRF. `/auth/google/callback` verifies the state, exchanges the code for an access token, fetches the user's Google profile, then follows the three-way lookup: match by `google_id` (returning user) → match by `email` (link existing account) → create new account. The `derive_username` helper turns a Google display name like "Nithin Vin" into `nithinvin`, and `unique_username` appends a random hex suffix if that name is already taken. The login route's dummy-hash check was updated to handle the case where `password_hash` is `NULL` for Google-only accounts.<br><br>**`login.html` + `signup.html`** — "Continue with Google" / "Sign up with Google" button with the real Google logo SVG (Google's brand guidelines require the exact four-colour logo, not a generic button). An "or" divider separates it from the form.<br><br>**`style.css`** — `.btn--google` uses a white background with a subtle shadow — this matches Google's own button design spec. `.auth-divider` uses CSS pseudo-elements for the horizontal lines around the "or" text. |

| json_block | {"language": "sql", "code": "-- migrate_google_oauth.sql\n--\n-- Run this ONCE on the existing database to add Google OAuth support.\n-- It adds email and google_id to the users table without dropping anything.\n--\n-- Usage:\n--   psql -U bookshelf_user -d bookshelf_db -h localhost -f deploy/migrate_google_oauth.sql\n\nBEGIN;\n\n-- email: nullable because existing username/password users have no email on record yet.\n-- Google OAuth users will always have one. UNIQUE so one Google account = one shelf.\nALTER TABLE users\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email     VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE,\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS google_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE;\n\n-- Fast lookup by google_id on every OAuth callback\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_google_id ON users(google_id);\n\n-- Fast lookup by email for account-linking logic\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email ON users(email);\n\nCOMMIT;\n", "filename": "/mnt/user-data/outputs/deploy/migrate_google_oauth.sql"} |

   SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True,\n    SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=\"Lax\",\n    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=os.environ.get(\"FORCE_HTTPS\", \"false\").lower() == \"true\",\n)\n\n# \u2500\u2500 hCaptcha \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nHCAPTCHA_SECRET     = os.environ.get(\"HCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY\", \"\")\nHCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY   = os.environ.get(\"HCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY\", \"\")\nHCAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL = \"https://api.hcaptcha.com/siteverify\"\n\ndef HCAPTCHA_SECRET, \"response\": token},\n            timeout=5,\n        )\n        return resp.json().get(\"success\", False)\n    except Exception:\n        return False\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Google OAuth config \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nGOOGLE_CLIENT_ID     = os.environ.get(\"GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID\", \"\")\nGOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET = os.environ.get(\"GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET\", \"\")\nGOOGLE_AUTH_URL      = \"https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth\"\nGOOGLE_TOKEN_URL     = \"https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token\"\nGOOGLE_USERINFO_URL  = \"https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/userinfo\"\nGOOGLE_SCOPES        = \"openid email profile\"\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 DB helpers \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\ndef dbname=os.environ[\"DB_NAME\"],\n            user=os.environ[\"DB_USER\"],\n            password=os.environ[\"DB_PASSWORD\"],\n            cursor_factory=RealDictCursor,\n        )\n    return g.db\n\n\n@app.teardown_appcontext\ndef close_db(error=None):\n    db = g.pop(\"db\", None)\n    if db is not None:\n        db.close()\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Auth helpers \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\ndef redirect(url_for(\"login\"))\n        return f(*args, **kwargs)\n    return decorated\n\n\ndef current_user_id():\n    return session.get(\"user_id\")\n\n\ndef set_session(user):\n    \"\"\"Populate session from a user row dict.\"\"\"\n    session[\"user_id\"]  = user[\"id\"]\n    session[\"username\"] = user[\"username\"]\n\n\ndef derive_username(name: str, email: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Turn a Google display name or email into a clean username candidate.\n    Strips non-alphanumeric chars. Falls back to the email local part.\n    \"\"\"\n    base = re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]\", \"\", name.lower()) if name else \"\"\n    if not base:\n        base = re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]\", \"\", email.split(\"@\")[0].lower())\n    return base[:40] or \"user\"\n\n\ndef unique_username(db, base: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Ensure username is unique. If taken, append a short random suffix.\n    \"\"\"\n    candidate = base\n    for _ in range(10):\n        with db.cursor() as cur:\n            cur.execute(\"SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = | new_str | -- migrate_google_oauth.sql<br>--<br>-- Run this ONCE on the existing database to add Google OAuth support.<br>-- It adds email and google_id to the users table without dropping anything.<br>--<br>-- Usage:<br>--   psql -U bookshelf_user -d bookshelf_db -h localhost -f deploy/migrate_google_oauth.sql<br><br>BEGIN;<br><br>-- Google-only users have no password, so the NOT NULL constraint must be dropped.<br>-- Existing password users are unaffected — their hash is already stored.<br>ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN password_hash DROP NOT NULL;<br><br>-- email: nullable because existing username/password users have no email on record yet.<br>-- Google OAuth users will always have one. UNIQUE so one Google account = one shelf.<br>ALTER TABLE users<br>    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email     VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE,<br>    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS google_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE;<br><br>-- Fast lookup by google_id on every OAuth callback<br>CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_google_id ON users(google_id);<br><br>-- Fast lookup by email for account-linking logic<br>CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email ON users(email);<br><br>COMMIT; |
| old_str | -- migrate_google_oauth.sql<br>--<br>-- Run this ONCE on the existing database to add Google OAuth support.<br>-- It adds email and google_id to the users table without dropping anything.<br>--<br>-- Usage:<br>--   psql -U bookshelf_user -d bookshelf_db -h localhost -f deploy/migrate_google_oauth.sql<br><br>BEGIN;<br><br>-- email: nullable because existing username/password users have no email on record yet.<br>-- Google OAuth users will always have one. UNIQUE so one Google account = one shelf.<br>ALTER TABLE users<br>    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email     VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE,<br>    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS google_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE;<br><br>-- Fast lookup by google_id on every OAuth callback<br>CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_google_id ON users(google_id);<br><br>-- Fast lookup by email for account-linking logic<br>CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email ON users(email);<br><br>COMMIT; |

Push and deploy<br>git add .<br>git commit -m "Add friends system with shelf sharing"<br>git push origin main<br>./deploy/deploy.sh<br>```<br><br>---<br><br>Here's what was built and the reasoning behind each decision:<br><br>**`migrate_friends.sql` — new table**<br><br>A single `friendships` table with `requester_id`, `addressee_id`, and `status` (`pending` or `accepted`). Two DB constraints do the heavy lifting: `UNIQUE(requester_id, addressee_id)` prevents duplicate requests, and `CHECK(requester_id <> addressee_id)` prevents self-friending at the database level — not just in Python. The direction of the row is preserved (requester vs addressee) so the app knows who sent it.<br><br>**`app.py` — six new routes and two helpers**<br><br>`friendship_status()` does a single query covering both directions of the relationship and returns one of four states: `accepted`, `pending_sent`, `pending_received`, or `None`. This drives both the search results page and the send-request guard. `are_friends()` is a tighter check used only in `view_shelf` to gate access. The `@app.context_processor` `inject_pending_count()` runs on every request when a user is logged in — it queries the count of incoming pending requests and injects it as `{{ pending_count }}` into every template automatically, without needing to pass it manually from each route. `view_shelf` has an explicit ownership guard: even if you know someone's user ID, you cannot view their shelf unless `are_friends()` returns true.<br><br>**`base.html`** — Friends link with a `{{ pending_count }}` badge. The badge only renders when count > 0 so the nav stays clean when there are no pending requests.<br><br>**Three new templates:**<br>- `friends.html` — three panels: incoming requests (accept/decline), accepted friends (view shelf / remove), outgoing sent requests (cancel). Incoming panel only renders if there are actual requests.<br>- `user_search.html` — GET form so the search query is in the URL and bookmarkable. Each result shows the current relationship status and the appropriate action button.<br>- `shelf_view.html` — reuses the same book card design and `list.js` for search/sort, but with no edit/delete buttons and a green spine stripe to visually distinguish it from your own shelf. |

2.0 (side-by-side)\n        Accounts are linked when Google email matches an existing user's email.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport re\nimport secrets\nimport bcrypt\nimport psycopg2\nimport requests as http_requests\nfrom psycopg2.extras import RealDictCursor\nfrom functools import wraps\nfrom flask import (\n    Flask, g, session,\n    render_template, request, redirect, url_for, flash\n)\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\n\napp = Flask(__name__)\napp.secret_key = os.environ[\"SECRET_KEY\"]\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Session cookie security \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\napp.config.update(\n    SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True,\n    SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=\"Lax\",\n    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=os.environ.get(\"FORCE_HTTPS\", \"false\").lower() == \"true\",\n)\n\n# \u2500\u2500 hCaptcha \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nHCAPTCHA_SECRET     = os.environ.get(\"HCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY\", \"\")\nHCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY   = os.environ.get(\"HCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY\", \"\")\nHCAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL = \"https://api.hcaptcha.com/siteverify\"\n\ndef verify_hcaptcha(token: str) -> bool:\n    if not token:\n        return False\n    try:\n        resp = http_requests.post(\n            HCAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL,\n            data={\"secret\": HCAPTCHA_SECRET, \"response\": token},\n            timeout=5,\n        )\n        return resp.json().get(\"success\", False)\n    except Exception:\n        return False\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Google OAuth config \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nGOOGLE_CLIENT_ID     = os.environ.get(\"GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID\", \"\")\nGOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET = os.environ.get(\"GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET\", \"\")\nGOOGLE_AUTH_URL      = \"https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth\"\nGOOGLE_TOKEN_URL     = \"https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token\"\nGOOGLE_USERINFO_URL  = \"https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/userinfo\"\nGOOGLE_SCOPES        = \"openid email profile\"\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 DB helpers \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\ndef dbname=os.environ[\"DB_NAME\"],\n            user=os.environ[\"DB_USER\"],\n            password=os.environ[\"DB_PASSWORD\"],\n            cursor_factory=RealDictCursor,\n        )\n    return g.db\n\n\n@app.teardown_appcontext\ndef close_db(error=None):\n    db = g.pop(\"db\", None)\n    if db is not None:\n        db.close()\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Auth helpers | json_block | {"language": "sql", "code": "-- migrate_friends.sql\n--\n-- Adds the friendships table for friend requests and accepted friendships.\n-- Run ONCE on the existing database:\n--   psql -U bookshelf_user -d bookshelf_db -h localhost -f deploy/migrate_friends.sql\n\nBEGIN;\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS friendships (\n    id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n    requester_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    addressee_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    status      VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'\n                CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'accepted')),\n    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    -- Prevent duplicate requests in either direction\n    CONSTRAINT no_duplicate_requests UNIQUE (requester_id, addressee_id),\n    -- Prevent self-friending\n    CONSTRAINT no_self_friendship    CHECK  (requester_id <> addressee_id)\n);\n\n-- Fast lookups for \"show me all my pending/accepted friendships\"\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_friends_requester ON friendships(requester_id, status);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_friends_addressee ON friendships(addressee_id, status);\n\nCOMMIT;\n", "filename": "/mnt/user-data/outputs/deploy/migrate_friends.sql"} |
| type | json_block |

        \"SELECT title FROM books WHERE id = %s AND user_id = %s;\",\n            (book_id, current_user_id()),\n        )\n        book = cur.fetchone()\n        if book:\n Accepted friends list\n      2. Pending incoming requests (with Accept / Decline buttons)\n      3. Pending outgoing requests\n    \"\"\"\n    me = current_user_id()\n    db = get_db()\n\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        # Accepted friends \u2014 return the OTHER user's details\n        cur.execute(\n            \"\"\"SELECT u.id, u.username\n               FROM friendships f\n               JOIN users u ON u.id = CASE\n                   WHEN f.requester_id = %s THEN f.addressee_id\n                   ELSE f.requester_id END\n               WHERE (f.requester_id = %s OR f.addressee_id = %s)\n                 AND f.status = 'accepted'\n               ORDER BY u.username;\"\"\",\n            (me, me, me),\n        )\n        accepted = cur.fetchall()\n\n        # Incoming pending requests\n        cur.execute(\n            \"\"\"SELECT f.id AS friendship_id, u.id, u.username\n               FROM friendships f\n               JOIN users u ON u.id = f.requester_id\n               WHERE f.addressee_id = %s AND f.status = 'pending'\n               ORDER BY f.created_at DESC;\"\"\",\n            (me,),\n        )\n        incoming = cur.fetchall()\n\n        # Outgoing pending requests\n        cur.execute(\n            \"\"\"SELECT f.id AS friendship_id, u.id, u.username\n               FROM friendships f\n               JOIN users u ON u.id = f.addressee_id\n               WHERE f.requester_id = %s AND f.status = 'pending'\n               ORDER BY f.created_at DESC;\"\"\",\n            (me,),\n        )\n        outgoing = cur.fetchall()\n\n    return render_template(\"friends.html\",\n                           accepted=accepted,\n                           incoming=incoming,\n                           outgoing=outgoing)\n\n\n@app.route(\"/users/search\")\n@login_required\ndef user_search():\n    \"\"\"Search users by username; returns relationship status for each result.\"\"\"\n    query = request.args.get(\"q\", \"\").strip().lower()\n    me    = current_user_id()\n    results = []\n\n    if query and len(query) >= 2:\n        db = get_db()\n        with db.cursor() as cur:\n            cur.execute(\n                \"\"\"SELECT id, username FROM users\n                   WHERE username ILIKE %s AND id <> %s\n                   ORDER BY username LIMIT 20;\"\"\",\n                (f\"%{query}%\", me),\n            )\n            users = cur.fetchall()\n\n        for u in users:\n            status = friendship_status(db, me, u[\"id\"])\n            results.append({**u, \"status\": status})\n\n    return render_template(\"user_search.html\", query=query, results=results)\n\n\n@app.route(\"/friends/request/<int:addressee_id>\", methods=[\"POST\"])\n@login_required\ndef send_request(addressee_id):\n    me = current_user_id()\n    if me == addressee_id:\n        flash(\"You can't friend yourself.\", \"error\")\n        return redirect(url_for(\"user_search\"))\n\n    db = get_db()\n    # Check the target user exists\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        cur.execute(\"SELECT username FROM users WHERE id = %s;\", (addressee_id,))\n        target = cur.fetchone()\n    if not target:\n        flash(\"User not found.\", \"error\")\n        return redirect(url_for(\"user_search\"))\n\n    # Check no relationship already exists\n    existing = friendship_status(db, me, addressee_id)\n    if existing:\n        flash(\"A friend request already exists with this user.\", \"info\")\n        return redirect(url_for(\"user_search\", q=request.form.get(\"q\", \"\")))\n\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        cur.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO friendships (requester_id, addressee_id) VALUES (%s, %s);\",\n            (me, addressee_id),\n        )\n    db.commit()\n    flash(f\"Friend request sent to {target['username']}.\", \"success\")\n    return redirect(url_for(\"user_search\", q=request.form.get(\"q\", \"\")))\n\n\n@app.route(\"/friends/accept/<int:friendship_id>\", methods=[\"POST\"])\n@login_required\ndef accept_request(friendship_id):\n    me = current_user_id()\n    db = get_db()\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        cur.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM friendships WHERE id = %s AND addressee_id = %s AND status = 'pending';\",\n            (friendship_id, me),\n        )\n        row = cur.fetchone()\n\n    if not row:\n        flash(\"Request not found.\", \"error\")\n        return redirect(url_for(\"friends\"))\n\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        cur.execute(\n            \"UPDATE friendships SET status = 'accepted' WHERE id = %s;\",\n            (friendship_id,),\n        )\n    db.commit()\n\n    # Look up who sent it so we can greet by name\n    db2 = get_db()\n    with db2.cursor() as cur:\n        cur.execute(\"SELECT username FROM users WHERE id = %s;\", (row[\"requester_id\"],))\n        sender = cur.fetchone()\n    flash(f\"You and {sender['username']} are now friends!\", \"success\")\n    return redirect(url_for(\"friends\"))\n\n\n@app.route(\"/friends/decline/<int:friendship_id>\", methods=[\"POST\"])\n@login_required\ndef decline_request(friendship_id):\n    \"\"\"Decline or cancel a request \u2014 deletes the row entirely.\"\"\"\n    me = current_user_id()\n    db = get_db()\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        # Allow both the addressee (decline) and requester (cancel) to delete\n        cur.execute(\n            \"\"\"DELETE FROM friendships\n               WHERE id = %s\n                 AND (addressee_id = %s OR requester_id = %s);\"\"\",\n            (friendship_id, me, me),\n        )\n    db.commit()\n    flash(\"Friend request removed.\", \"info\")\n    return redirect(url_for(\"friends\"))\n\n\n@app.route(\"/friends/remove/<int:friend_id>\", methods=[\"POST\"])\n@login_required\ndef remove_friend(friend_id):\n    me = current_user_id()\n    db = get_db()\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        cur.execute(\n            \"\"\"DELETE FROM friendships\n               WHERE status = 'accepted'\n                 AND ((requester_id = %s AND addressee_id = %s)\n                   OR (requester_id = %s AND addressee_id = %s));\"\"\",\n            (me, friend_id, friend_id, me),\n        )\n    db.commit()\n    flash(\"Friend removed.\", \"info\")\n    return redirect(url_for(\"friends\"))\n\n\n@app.route(\"/shelf/<int:user_id>\")\n@login_required\ndef view_shelf(user_id):\n    \"\"\"\n    Read-only view of a friend's shelf.\n    Only accessible if the two users are accepted friends.\n    \"\"\"\n    me = current_user_id()\n    if me == user_id:\n        return redirect(url_for(\"index\"))\n\n    db = get_db()\n\n    # Guard: must be accepted friends\n    if not are_friends(db, me, user_id):\n        flash(\"You can only view shelves of your friends.\", \"error\")\n        return redirect(url_for(\"friends\"))\n\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        cur.execute(\"SELECT username FROM users WHERE id = %s;\", (user_id,))\n        owner = cur.fetchone()\n\n    if not owner:\n        flash(\"User not found.\", \"error\")\n        return redirect(url_for(\"friends\"))\n\n    with db.cursor() as cur:\n        cur.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM books WHERE user_id = %s ORDER BY title ASC;\",\n            (user_id,),\n        )\n        books = cur.fetchall()\n\n    return render_template(\"shelf_view.html\", books=books, owner=owner)\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Health \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\n@app.route(\"/health\")\ndef health():\n    return {\"status\": \"ok\"}, 200\n\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Entry point \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    app.run(debug=(os.environ.get(\"FLASK_ENV\") == \"development\"))\nPYEOF"} |

-f \"$ENV_FILE\" ]; then\n    echo \"[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] ERROR: $ENV_FILE not found.\" \| tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n_env_val() {\n    grep -E \"^${1}=\" \"$ENV_FILE\" \| head -n1 \| sed \"s/^${1}=//\" \| tr -d '\"'\"'\"' '\n}\n\nDB_NAME=$(_env_val DB_NAME)\nDB_USER=$(_env_val DB_USER)\nDB_PASSWORD=$(_env_val DB_PASSWORD)\nDB_HOST=$(_env_val DB_HOST)\nDB_PORT=$(_env_val DB_PORT)\n\nif [ -z \"$DB_NAME\" ] \|\| [ -z \"$DB_USER\" ]; then\n    echo \"[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] ERROR: DB_NAME or DB_USER missing in $ENV_FILE.\" \| tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Create backup directory if it doesn't exist \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nmkdir -p \"$BACKUP_DIR\"\nchmod 700 \"$BACKUP_DIR\"   # only root can read backup files\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Run pg_dump and compress \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\necho \"[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] Starting backup \u2192 $BACKUP_FILE\" >> \"$LOG_FILE\"\n\nPGPASSWORD=\"$DB_PASSWORD\" pg_dump \\\n    --host=\"$DB_HOST\" \\\n    --port=\"$DB_PORT\" \\\n    --username=\"$DB_USER\" \\\n    --format=plain \\\n    --no-password \\\n    \"$DB_NAME\" \\\n    \| gzip -9 > \"$BACKUP_FILE\"\n\n# Verify the file was created and is non-empty\nif [ ! -s \"$BACKUP_FILE\" ]; then\n    echo \"[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] ERROR: Backup file is empty or missing.\" \| tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nSIZE=$(du -sh \"$BACKUP_FILE\" \| cut -f1)\necho \"[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] Backup complete. Size: $SIZE\" >> \"$LOG_FILE\"\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Delete backups older than KEEP_DAYS \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nDELETED=$(find \"$BACKUP_DIR\" \\\n    -maxdepth 1 \\\n    -name \"bookshelf_*.sql.gz\" \\\n    -mtime \"+${KEEP_DAYS}\" \\\n    -print \\\n    -delete \\\n    \| wc -l)\n\nif [ \"$DELETED\" -gt 0 ]; then\n    echo \"[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] Deleted $DELETED backup(s) older than ${KEEP_DAYS} days.\" >> \"$LOG_FILE\"\nfi\n\n# \u2500\u2500 List retained backups \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\necho \"[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] Retained backups:\" >> \"$LOG_FILE\"\nfind \"$BACKUP_DIR\" -maxdepth 1 -name \"bookshelf_*.sql.gz\" \\\n    \| sort \| while read -r f; do\n    echo \"    $(basename \"$f\")  ($(du -sh \"$f\" \| cut -f1))\" >> \"$LOG_FILE\"\ndone\n\necho \"---\" >> \"$LOG_FILE\"\n", "filename": "/mnt/user-data/outputs/deploy/backup_db.sh"} |

All current data will be lost.\n#          Stop the bookshelf service before restoring.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nENV_FILE=\"/srv/bookshelf/.env\"\nBACKUP_FILE=\"${1:-}\"\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Validate input \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nif [ -z \"$BACKUP_FILE\" ]; then\n    echo \"Usage: sudo bash restore_db.sh <backup_file>\"\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"Available backups:\"\n    ls -lh /srv/backups/bookshelf/*.sql.gz 2>/dev/null \|\| echo \"  (none found)\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"$BACKUP_FILE\" ]; then\n    echo \"ERROR: File not found: $BACKUP_FILE\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Read DB credentials \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n_env_val() {\n    grep -E \"^${1}=\" \"$ENV_FILE\" \| head -n1 \| sed \"s/^${1}=//\" \| tr -d '\"'\"'\"' '\n}\n\nDB_NAME=$(_env_val DB_NAME)\nDB_USER=$(_env_val DB_USER)\nDB_PASSWORD=$(_env_val DB_PASSWORD)\nDB_HOST=$(_env_val DB_HOST)\nDB_PORT=$(_env_val DB_PORT)\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Confirm \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\necho \"========================================================\"\necho \"  WARNING: This will OVERWRITE the current database.\"\necho \"  Database : $DB_NAME\"\necho \"  Backup   : $(basename \"$BACKUP_FILE\")\"\necho \"========================================================\"\nread -p \"  Type 'yes' to continue: \" confirm\n[ \"$confirm\" = \"yes\" ] \|\| { echo \"Aborted.\"; exit 0; }\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Stop service so no writes happen during restore \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\necho \"--> Stopping bookshelf service...\"\nsystemctl stop bookshelf \|\| true\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Restore \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\necho \"--> Restoring from $BACKUP_FILE ...\"\nPGPASSWORD=\"$DB_PASSWORD\" gunzip -c \"$BACKUP_FILE\" \\\n    \| psql \\\n        --host=\"$DB_HOST\" \\\n        --port=\"$DB_PORT\" \\\n        --username=\"$DB_USER\" \\\n        --dbname=\"$DB_NAME\" \\\n        --no-password \\\n        --quiet\n\necho \"--> Restore complete.\"\n\n# \u2500\u2500 Restart service \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\necho \"--> Restarting bookshelf service...\"\nsystemctl start bookshelf\nsystemctl is-active --quiet bookshelf \\\n    && echo \"--> Service is running.\" \\\n    \|\| echo \"--> WARNING: Service failed to start. Check: journalctl -u bookshelf -n 30\"\n", "filename": "/mnt/user-data/outputs/deploy/restore_db.sh"} |

Open root's crontab<br>sudo crontab -e<br>```<br><br>Add this one line — runs the backup every day at 2 AM:<br><br>```<br>0 2 * * * /bin/bash /srv/bookshelf/deploy/backup_db.sh >> /var/log/bookshelf/backup.log 2>&1<br>```<br><br>Save and exit (`:wq` in vim, `Ctrl+O` then `Ctrl+X` in nano).<br><br>**Verify it was saved:**<br>```bash<br>sudo crontab -l<br>```<br><br>**Test the script runs without errors right now:**<br>```bash<br>sudo bash /srv/bookshelf/deploy/backup_db.sh<br>```<br><br>**Check the log after:**<br>```bash<br>tail -20 /var/log/bookshelf/backup.log<br>```<br><br>**Check backups exist:**<br>```bash<br>ls -lh /srv/backups/bookshelf/<br>```<br><br>That's it. The cron runs daily at 2 AM, keeps the last 3 days, and logs everything to the same log file you already have. To change retention, edit `KEEP_DAYS` at the top of `backup_db.sh`. |
